headline: All seven majors sit below their 200-day lines while fear reads 27, and whale wallets keep pulling coin off exchanges anyway
paragraphs: Start with regime, because it's unanimous today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all below their 200-day moving averages, none carry a golden cross, and every one of them sits well off its 12-month high, from BTC's 49.2% drawdown to ADA's stark 81.0%. When seven-for-seven line up on the same side of the 200-day, that's not noise, that's the regime. Nothing here is fighting the tape from below.

Momentum tells a more mixed story than trend does, and that gap is worth naming. BTC's RSI sits at 45.3 with MACD below signal, matched bearish. But SOL, BNB and DOGE all show MACD above signal (bullish crosses) while still trapped under their 200-day averages, and BNB's RSI at 63.3 is pushing toward overbought inside a downtrend. That's momentum resting or flickering upward inside a structure that hasn't turned. XRP is the opposite case: RSI at 36.0, the weakest reading on the board, and it's down 7.2% over the last seven days versus BTC's flat -0.13%, so the divergence there runs against the grain, not with it.

Positioning is where the fragility shows up plainest. Long/short ratios are stacked heavily long across the board (BTC 1.89, SOL 2.22, XRP 3.33, DOGE 4.93), meaning far more accounts are betting up than down. Funding is positive everywhere, with BTC, ETH and XRP all paying an annualized 11.0% for longs to hold their bets, DOGE close behind at 9.6%. That's a crowd paying up to stay long into a market that's below trend on every asset. The liquidation tape backs up the lean: BTC saw $2.42M in long liquidations against $1.19M in shorts over 23 hours, DOGE's long/short ratio of 4.93 came with $243K in long liquidations versus $357K in shorts, longs getting squeezed both ways depending on the asset. ETH is the exception worth flagging, shorts took the bigger hit there ($5.88M liquidated versus $3.89M in longs) even with funding also positive, a genuine mismatch between who's paying and who's getting flushed.

Flows cut against the mood. BTC spot ETFs posted a modest $7.8M net inflow on 11 Aug 2026, small on its own, but the five-session net for BTC ETFs runs $346.9M positive and ETH ETFs sit at $186.2M over the same window, even though ETH's own latest print was a $1.7M outflow. Same-direction-day counts (1 for BTC, 2 for ETH) are too short to call this a trend, but the five-day totals are unambiguous in sign. Layer on whale activity: $310.4M net moved off exchanges in the last 48 hours, split $254.3M in BTC and $56.2M in ETH, with the weekly series showing two sessions near +$1.2B off-exchange before the most recent reading flipped to -$724.9M onto exchanges. That's not a straight line, it's a coin flip with the last print net negative, but the 48-hour snapshot and the ETF five-day nets both point the same way: toward accumulation, not distribution. Stablecoin float, meanwhile, is essentially flat, down just 0.98% over 30 days to $306.4B, so the dry powder hasn't meaningfully grown or shrunk.

Sentiment sits at 27, labeled Fear, near the bottom of its own 30-day range of 22 to 33. That's a crowd that feels bad. The tape doesn't fully agree: funding is positive and leveraged accounts are heavily long, which isn't how fear usually shows up in derivatives, and whale wallets are net pulling coin into cold storage over both the 48-hour and recent multi-day windows even as the fear gauge stays low. When the mood and the money disagree this openly, that disagreement is the story, not a footnote.

What to watch from here: whether any major reclaims its 200-day average (none have), whether BTC funding flips negative (it's been positive at 11.0% annualized), and whether the whale weekly series prints a second consecutive net-onto-exchange session after the last one broke the streak of positive weeks. Any of those would mark a genuine change in what this data is showing.
